fail_reasons: SC-10(4) fail-closed direction violated: the two NEW caps introduced by __verb_brace_matches() (512-char token cap, 64-unit __VERB_BRACE_BUDGET) fall OPEN when exceeded. Measured allow + real destruction of a synthetic control-plane file in an isolated lab: `{f,g,g x70}ind .claude -delete` (budget) and `{f,<600 chars>}ind .claude -delete` (512-char cap). No boundary test was shipped in the same commit, which SC-10(4) requires verbatim. This is the same defect class the 28th verdict failed F65 for.

SC-10(6) all-arming-sites rule violated for the new brace check: it was wired to 3 of the 4 known sites; the 4th (__note_opaque_verb()/__scan_opaque_verb_matches(), substitution/backtick span interior) was not. Measured: `` `{f,g}ind .claude -delete` `` and `$({f,g}ind .claude -delete)` are allow + real deletion, while the substitution-only sibling `` `f$(true)ind .claude -delete` `` is correctly ask -- exactly the asymmetry the 35th verdict failed on.

AUDIT-6 axis is not closed when a brace-split verb token also contains a substitution or a parameter expansion: `{f,g}in$(true)d .claude -delete` and `{f,g}in${Z}d .claude -delete` are allow + real deletion. Both constructs are individually claimed closed (36th verdict / this commit); the combination is neither closed nor registered as residual.

QA-1 closure is false WITHIN its own declared narrow scope for the -delete predicate position: `D=-delete; find .claude $D` and `D=-delete; find hooks $D` are allow + real deletion, although the preceding segment is exactly `VAR=literalword` and the token is exactly `$VAR`. Root cause is SC-10(6) again: __apply_pending_assignment() was wired to the two loops inside __scan_one_segment_for_cp_delete() but NOT to pure_read_only()'s own find pre-filter, which is the wider gate that prevents scan_control_plane_delete() from ever being called -- the exact structural trap the commit's own comment at hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:940-968 describes for braces and then fails to apply to the assignment idiom. sprint-51.json `assign_then_invoke_verb.status` claims closure for the '피연산자 자리·find/-delete 술어 자리 모두', which the measurement contradicts.
issues: [security][critical][confidence:high] __VERB_BRACE_BUDGET exhaustion is fail-open at verb position. `{f,g,g,...(70 alternatives)}ind .claude -delete` -> firewall allow; isolated lab (fresh mktemp dir, synthetic .claude/settings.json) -> .claude/settings.json DESTROYED. The 20-alternative control of the same shape is ask, so the boundary is exactly the budget. __verb_brace_matches_impl() returns 1 ('not decided by this check') on budget exhaustion, and unlike the operand judge there is no downstream judge for the verb position, so 'not decided' collapses to allow.

[security][critical][confidence:high] The new 512-char token cap in __verb_brace_matches_impl() is fail-open the same way: `{f,<600 x 'g'>}ind .claude -delete` -> allow + real deletion in the lab. Sibling caps in this file (__control_plane_location_impl 512, SEGMENT_UNSAFE 2048, the 28th verdict's dash-token cap after 3a7c573) all fall the other way.

[security][critical][confidence:high] Brace-split verbs are not checked inside substitution/backtick spans: `` `{f,g}ind .claude -delete` `` and `$({f,g}ind .claude -delete)` -> allow + real deletion. `` `find .claude -delete` `` (literal verb, same wrapper) is ask, and `` `f$(true)ind .claude -delete` `` (36th verdict cell) is ask -- so only the brace variant leaks. 4th arming site of SC-10(6) missed.

[security][critical][confidence:high] Brace expansion combined with command substitution or parameter expansion inside one verb token defeats both mechanisms: `{f,g}in$(true)d .claude -delete`, `{f,g}in${Z}d .claude -delete` -> allow + real deletion. __verb_brace_matches_impl() compares the brace leaves as raw literals (no __mask_opaque_spans/__strip_dollar_brace on the leaves), and the masking path in turn never re-expands braces.

[security][critical][confidence:high] QA-1 in-scope leak at the -delete predicate position: `D=-delete; find .claude $D` -> allow + .claude/settings.json DESTROYED; `D=-delete; find hooks $D` -> allow + hooks/hooks.json DESTROYED. The capture regex `^VAR=[A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+$` does accept `-delete`, and __apply_pending_assignment() would substitute it, but pure_read_only()'s find branch classifies the segment as pure-read (its three literal `-delete` substring checks and the new `{` guard all miss) and short-circuits the whole control-plane scan. Control: `P=.claude; find $P -delete` (literal predicate present) is correctly ask.

[security][high][confidence:high] Multi-word brace verb expansions are blocked on this darwin box only by BSD rm's refusal to permute options, not by the firewall: `{r,x}$(true)m -rf .claude`, `r$(true){m,x} -rf .claude`, `{r,x}${Z}m -rf .claude` are all allow and expand to `rm <junk> -rf .claude`, which is a no-op under BSD rm but deletes under GNU rm (Linux CI, containers, remote hosts). The lab therefore shows 'present' for these, but the firewall decision is still wrong and the same shapes with `find` (which tolerates extra paths) do destroy on this machine.

[security][high][confidence:medium] Pre-existing (present at d8107d4 too, NOT a regression of this commit, reported under the Reporting Policy): `eval "rm -rf .claude"` and `eval "{r..r}m -rf .claude"` are allow + real deletion. `eval` is a shell-text delivery mechanism with no `-c`-shaped flag, so __has_shell_code_flag() never fires; wrapper_code_delivery_mechanism enumerates env -S / herestring / pipe but not `eval`. Recommend registering it in _residual_risk_AC11 or closing it.

[security][medium][confidence:medium] Pre-existing, not attributable to this commit: an ancestor directory of a control-plane file is not a control-plane operand. `rm -rf hooks`, `find hooks -delete` and `rm -rf .` are all allow, and `find hooks -delete` destroyed hooks/hooks.json in the lab, while `find hooks/hooks.json -delete` is ask. This is why the brace probe `{f,g}ind hooks -delete` allowed -- the brace check is not at fault there.

[code_quality][medium][confidence:high] The comment above __verb_brace_matches_impl() promises that the unexpandable/over-budget verb subcase 'declared residual로 남는다(정리해 sprint-51.json 에 등록)'. No such entry exists in sprint-51.json: _residual_risk_AC11 has no key for it and the AUDIT-6 status text only narrates the return-direction flip. SC-10(7) (residual attribution rule, created by the 36th round) requires the contract entry to exist before the behaviour is treated as intended.

[code_quality][low][confidence:high] pure_read_only()'s brace guard `[[ "$__seg_norm" == *'{'* ]] && return 1` is applied to __seg_norm (quotes/backslashes stripped) while the three predicate checks above it are applied to three different strings ($seg, $__seg_norm, $__seg_stripped). A brace introduced only in the masked/stripped form would be missed. Low impact today, but the four copies keep drifting apart -- the same drift that produced AUDIT-4 and the 34th/35th verdicts.

[error_handling][high][confidence:high] The two new caps have no boundary tests at all (no 511/512/513-char pair, no 64/65-alternative pair), so the direction they fall is untested. SC-10(4) makes such a test mandatory in the same commit that adds a cap.

[test_coverage][medium][confidence:high] The six new bats tests assert only the instance lists from the audit reports plus friction controls. Per SC-9's positive criterion, an axis counts as checked only when a generation rule (element pools x positions x nesting) is implemented as a test. A rule of the shape {brace, substitution, parameter expansion} x {bare, backtick span, $( ) span} x {verb, predicate} would have caught four of the five findings above; the existing tests exercise exactly one cell of that product per row.

[test_coverage][low][confidence:high] The 36th verdict already noted that the 30-cell/15-cell sweeps live only in scratchpad repro scripts and were never promoted to committed bats tests; the 37th round's repro script repeats the pattern (66 cells, none committed).

[functionality][low][confidence:high] Reproduction bookkeeping: the prompt states the pre-fix hook yields 24 mismatches, but re-running the current repro script against d8107d4 gives 28 -- the four quoted-literal cells (V="rm"/V='rm'/etc.) were added to the script after repro-before.txt was recorded. No impact on the verdict; the recorded file should be regenerated so before/after are comparable.

[functionality][info][confidence:high] What DOES work and was independently re-measured: all 14 AUDIT-6 bare cells, the 3 operand-interception regression cells (`rm -rf x{1..a}` etc.), all 16 QA-1 adjacent cells, all 13 friction controls, and all 6 of the 35th/36th substitution-split cells behave as specified (repro RESULT mismatches=0). __VERB_BRACE_BUDGET is genuinely a separate global from __BRACE_BUDGET (hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh:1468 vs 1540) and __capture_pending_assignment() does reset on every non-assignment segment, so adjacency is real (`V=rm; echo; $V ...` stays allow, `echo hi; V=rm; $V hooks/hooks.json` is ask).

missing_criteria: sprint-51.json still has no standing generation rule for the splitting axis. The 35th, 36th and now the 37th round all recommend it. Concretely it should read as a product: {parameter expansion, command substitution, backtick, brace expansion, quote/backslash split} x {verb token, find token, -delete predicate token} x {bare segment, inside $( ), inside backticks, inside a shell wrapper} x {single construct, two constructs in one token}, with a test that enumerates the product rather than a per-instance list.

No criterion requires that a check answering 'not decided by this check' (return 1) be paired with a downstream judge that actually covers the position. __verb_brace_matches() is the first check in this file whose safe direction is 'defer', and deferral is only safe at operand position.
No criterion covers ancestor-directory operands (rm -rf hooks, find hooks -delete, rm -rf .) even though deleting the directory destroys the control-plane file inside it.
ambiguous_criteria: assign_then_invoke_verb.status claims the narrow scope is closed for '동사 자리·피연산자 자리·find/-delete 술어 자리 모두'. 'find/-delete 술어 자리' is ambiguous between 'find called via $V with a literal -delete' (true) and '-delete itself delivered via $V' (false). Rewrite as two separately checkable sentences.
security_criteria_insufficient: SC-10(6)'s site list is add-only but is maintained by hand in prose. Four rounds in a row (34th, 35th, 37th) failed on a missed site. Consider a mechanical check (invariant-guard) that greps for the set of functions implementing 'is this an armed delete verb' and asserts every new helper is called from all of them.
criteria_gaps.action_required: implementer: (1) make __verb_brace_matches()'s caps fail closed at verb position -- e.g. arm when an unexpandable/over-budget brace token sits at the segment's verb slot or is a dash-prefixed token in a find segment, keeping the 'defer' answer only for non-verb positions, and ship 511/512/513-char and 64/65-alternative boundary tests in the same commit; (2) wire the brace check into __note_opaque_verb()/__scan_opaque_verb_matches() (4th arming site) and apply __mask_opaque_spans()/__strip_dollar_brace() to each brace leaf before comparison so brace x substitution combinations are covered; (3) wire __apply_pending_assignment() (or an equivalent segment-text rewrite) into pure_read_only()'s find pre-filter so a $VAR-delivered -delete cannot short-circuit the whole scan; (4) register the residuals the code comments already promise (unexpandable brace verb, eval as a code-delivery mechanism, ancestor-directory operands) in _residual_risk_AC11 per SC-10(7); (5) promote the generation-rule sweep to committed bats tests.

recommended_fix.priority_2: SC-10(6) completion for both new checks: brace -> 4th site (opaque spans) and leaf-level masking; pending assignment -> pure_read_only's find pre-filter.
recommended_fix.priority_3: Contract truthfulness: downgrade the AUDIT-6 and assign_then_invoke_verb closure claims to the subset actually measured, and register the promised residuals.
